translationRepairs: In spring of the first year of the Xianhe era (326), on the dinghai day of the second month, the court proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted the new reign title, ordered five days of public feasting, distributed a hu of grain each to widowers, widows, orphans, and the elderly, and remitted one year of taxes and labor service within a hundred li of the capital.

In spring of the first year of the Xianhe era (326), on the dinghai day of the second month, the court proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted the new reign title, ordered five days of public feasting, distributed rice to widowers, widows, orphans, and the elderly at the rate of one hu for every two persons, and remitted one year of taxes and labor service within a hundred li of the capital.
二人斛 is a two-person ration of one hu, so the original “a hu … each” invents a per-person grant; the replacement states the rate correctly and keeps the rest of the sentence.

On the guihai day of the sixth month Liu Xia, duke of Quanling—holder of the insignia of authority, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, supervisor of all forces north of the Huai, north gentlemans-household general, and inspector of Xuzhou—passed away.

On the guihai day of the sixth month Liu Xia, duke of Quanling—holder of the insignia of authority, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, supervisor of all forces north of the Huai, General of the North Gentlemen of the Household, and inspector of Xuzhou—passed away.
北中郎將 is the office General of the North Gentlemen of the Household; “north gentlemans-household general” is ungrammatical and obscures the title.

On the guiyou day Xi Jian, general of chariots and cavalry, was ordered to take charge of Xuzhou as well, while Guo Mo, general who conquers the caitiffs, was named north gentlemans-household general, granted the credential staff, and put in command of the armies north of the Huai.

On the guiyou day Xi Jian, general of chariots and cavalry, was ordered to take charge of Xuzhou as well, while Guo Mo, general who conquers the caitiffs, was named General of the North Gentlemen of the Household, granted the credential staff, and put in command of the armies north of the Huai.
The same office 北中郎將 is again rendered with ungrammatical “gentlemans”; the capitalized office name matches the Chinese.

Borrowed Guard General Yu Liang's staff as campaign area commander, made Right Guard General Zhao Yin Champion General, Administrator of Liyang, ordered together with Left General Sima Liu to lead troops to resist Jun, battled at Cihu, Liu was defeated, died in it.

Yu Liang, Guard General, was granted the ceremonial staff as campaign commander-in-chief; Right Guard General Zhao Yin was made Champion General and Administrator of Liyang and, together with Left General Sima Liu, ordered to lead troops to resist Jun; they battled at Cihu; Liu was defeated and died in that battle.
假護軍將軍庾亮節爲征討都督 confers the jie on Yu Liang as campaign commander; “Borrowed Guard General Yu Liang's staff” reverses 假節 into borrowing his staff.
Borrowed Agile Cavalry General Zhong Ya's staff, led boat army, with Zhao Yin as van, in order to resist Jun.
Agile Cavalry General Zhong Ya was granted the ceremonial staff and led the boat army, with Zhao Yin as the van, in order to resist Jun.
假驍騎將軍鐘雅節 likewise grants Zhong Ya the jie; the original “Borrowed … Zhong Ya's staff” misreads the same construction.

In the first month of spring in the third year of Xianhe (328), Wen Qiao, general who pacifies the south, moved upstream to relieve the capital and halted at Xunyang, dispatching Wang Yanqi, Deng Yue of Xiyang, and Ji Mu of Poyang as his vanguard commanders.

In the first month of spring in the third year of Xianhe (328), Wen Qiao, general who pacifies the south, led troops to relieve the capital and halted at Xunyang, dispatching Wang Yanqi, Deng Yue of Xiyang, and Ji Mu of Poyang as his vanguard commanders.
帥師救京師 is leading troops to relieve the capital; “moved upstream” is not in the Chinese and is correctly removed.

Third year spring first month, General Who Pacifies the South Wen Qiao led troops to rescue the capital, halted at Xunyang, sent Supervisors Wang Yanqi, Administrator of Xiyang Deng Yue, Administrator of Poyang Ji Mu as van.

Third year spring first month, General Who Pacifies the South Wen Qiao led troops to rescue the capital, halted at Xunyang, sent Supervisor Wang Yanqi, Administrator of Xiyang Deng Yue, and Administrator of Poyang Ji Mu as van.
督護 titles only Wang Yanqi; Deng Yue and Ji Mu are 太守, so plural “Supervisors” wrongly spreads the office across all three.
On the gengxu day of the second month Su Jun reached Mount Jiang east of the capital.
On the gengxu day of the second month Su Jun reached Mount Jiang.
峻至于蔣山 names Mount Jiang only; “east of the capital” is an added gloss not present in the annal.
Borrowed General Who Commands the Army Bian Kun's staff, led six armies, and with Jun battled at Xiling, royal army was greatly defeated.
General Who Commands the Army Bian Kun was granted the ceremonial staff, led the six armies, and battled Jun at Xiling; the royal army was greatly defeated.
假領軍將軍卞壼節 is a grant of the jie to Bian Kun, not borrowing his staff.
On the renshen day Empress Mingmu was interred beside Emperor Ming at the Wuping mausoleum.
On the renshen day Empress Mingmu was interred at the Wuping mausoleum.
葬明穆皇后于武平陵 records only burial at Wuping; “beside Emperor Ming” is not in the Chinese.
On the yiwei day of the fifth month Su Jun forced the emperor to relocate to his stronghold at Stone Fort; the boy sovereign wept as he boarded the cart, and lamentation filled the palace.
On the yiwei day of the fifth month Su Jun forced the emperor to relocate to his stronghold at Stone Fort; the emperor wept as he boarded the cart, and lamentation filled the palace.
帝哀泣升車 calls him the emperor; “boy sovereign” is an added characterization not in 帝 or 天子.

In the first month of spring in the fourth year of Xianhe (329), while the emperor remained at Stone Fort, the rebel general Kuang Shu surrendered the Yuan walled park, and the court officials flocked to rejoin him.

In the first month of spring in the fourth year of Xianhe (329), while the emperor remained at Stone Fort, the rebel general Kuang Shu surrendered the Yuan walled park, and the court officials flocked there.
百官赴焉 points 焉 at the submitted 苑城, not at rejoining Kuang Shu in person.
An edict restored three years of rent and tax to commanderies and counties that had suffered bandits.
An edict remitted three years of rent and tax for commanderies and counties that had suffered bandits.
詔復遭賊郡縣租稅三年 is a three-year tax remission (復); “restored” inverts the fiscal measure.
Eighth month, Li Yao's generals Liu Yin and others led troops to invade Shi Sheng and halted at Yong.
Eighth month, Liu Yao's generals Liu Yin and others led troops to invade Shi Sheng and halted at Yong (the received surname graph is a corruption of Liu).

Received 利曜 is the same man as 劉曜 in the surrounding annal (太子毗…劉胤, then 盡滅劉氏); Wikisource keeps 利曜 while the intended surname is 劉, so rendering Li Yao as a separate person is wrong. The proposed literal note cannot keep Chinese graphs in the English replacement.
In the eighth month of autumn Shi Le declared himself emperor of Zhao and dispatched Guo Jing against Xiangyang.
In the eighth month of autumn Shi Le usurped the imperial throne and dispatched Guo Jing against Xiangyang.
僭卽皇帝位 is usurping the imperial throne; the sentence does not name Zhao, and “declared himself” softens 僭.
Zhou Fu, south gentlemans-household general, fell back to Wuchang, and the refugees from the central plains submitted en masse to Shi Le.
Zhou Fu, South Gentlemen of the Household General, fell back to Wuchang, and the refugees from the central plains submitted en masse to Shi Le.
南中郎將 is South Gentlemen of the Household General; “south gentlemans-household general” is ungrammatical.
Li Shou, a general under Li Xiong of Cheng, struck Badong and Jianping, forcing army supervisor Wuqiu Ao and Prefect Yang Qian to withdraw to Yidu.
Li Shou, a general under Li Xiong, struck Badong and Jianping, forcing army supervisor Wuqiu Ao and Prefect Yang Qian to withdraw to Yidu.
李雄將李壽 names Li Shou as Li Xiong’s general only; “of Cheng” is an added polity.
In the twelfth month Zhang Jun of Former Liang acknowledged Shi Le as overlord.
In the twelfth month Zhang Jun acknowledged Shi Le as overlord.
張駿稱臣于石勒 does not mention Former Liang; that polity name is interpolated.
In the third month Zhao Yin, west gentlemans-household general, and Kuang Shu, a staff gentleman of the minister of education, stormed Shi Le's riverside stronghold at Matou and took it.
In the third month Zhao Yin, West Gentlemen of the Household General, and Kuang Shu, a staff gentleman of the minister of education, stormed Shi Le's riverside stronghold at Matou and took it.
西中郎將 should be West Gentlemen of the Household General; “west gentlemans-household general” is ungrammatical.

Tao Kan, grand commandant, sent his son Tao Bin, an adviser on the staff of the general who pacifies the west, and Huan Xuan, south gentlemans-household general, against Guo Jing. They broke his army and took Fancheng.

Tao Kan, grand commandant, sent his son Tao Bin, an adviser on the staff of the general who pacifies the west, and Huan Xuan, South Gentlemen of the Household General, against Guo Jing. They broke his army and took Fancheng.
南中郎將桓宣 is the same office title; “south gentlemans-household general” is ungrammatical.
On the wuchen day of the seventh month Shi Le died. His son Shi Hong inherited the Zhao throne, while general Shi Cong brought the district of Qiao over to Jin.
On the wuchen day of the seventh month Shi Le died. His son Shi Hong inherited the false throne, while general Shi Cong brought the district of Qiao over to Jin.
嗣偽位 is succession to a false throne; “the Zhao throne” replaces 偽 with an unnamed polity.
In the fourth month of summer Shi Hu sent Shi Bin against Guo Quan at Mei and reduced the town.
In the fourth month of summer Shi Hong's general Shi Hu sent Shi Bin against Guo Quan at Mei and captured the town.
石弘將石季龍 makes Shi Hu Shi Hong’s general; dropping Shi Hong erases that command relation, and 陷之 is capture rather than a vague “reduced.”
In the eleventh month Shi Hu murdered Shi Hong and proclaimed himself heavenly king of Zhao.
In the eleventh month Shi Hu murdered Shi Hong and established himself as Heavenly King.
自立爲天王 does not name Zhao; “heavenly king of Zhao” interpolates the polity.
On the jiazi day of the second month the emperor personally offered the capping sacrifice to Confucius.
On the jiazi day of the second month the emperor personally performed the libation offering.
帝親釋奠 is the libation offering; Confucius and a “capping sacrifice” are not in this sentence (capping is 加元服 in the previous unit).
Shi Yu, serving Shi Hu, struck Zhonglu, and Wang Guo, south gentlemans-household general, fell back to defend Xiangyang.
Shi Yu, serving Shi Hu, struck Zhonglu, and Wang Guo, South Gentlemen of the Household General, fell back to defend Xiangyang.

south gentlemans-household general is ungrammatical, but “General of the Household Gentlemen of the South” scrambles the usual office order of 南中郎將; South Gentlemen of the Household General matches the Chinese and the chapter’s other 中郎將 renderings.
Second month, reckoning military-use tax rice, empty suspended more than five hundred thousand shi, from Masters of Writing Xie Bao si downward dismissed from office.
Second month, reckoning military-use tax rice, empty suspended more than five hundred thousand shi; from Masters of Writing Xie Bao downward, dismissed from office.
巳下 is 已下 “and those below,” not a given-name element si after Xie Bao.
The cadet branches of the Ji surname were enfeoffed to guard the Zhou royal house, a grace recorded in splendor on the Han rolls.
The cadet branches of the Ji surname were enfeoffed as Wei, a grace recorded in splendor on the Han rolls.

宗姬侯衛 is Ji cadets made the Wei marquisate, parallel to later 衛公, not “to guard the Zhou royal house”; “enfeoffed in Wei” is too locative, so the corrected line keeps the original cadet-branch phrasing and reads 侯衛 as enfeoffment as Wei.

In the sixth month the office of minister of education was retitled chancellor, and Grand Tutor Wang Dao was appointed to the post; the particle meaning by appointment was miscopied as the graph for second heavenly stem.
In the sixth month the office of minister of education was retitled chancellor, and Grand Tutor Wang Dao was appointed to the post.
The idiomatic sentence should translate the appointment; the 乙/以 collation note is not part of the annal’s meaning and does not belong in the English.
Sixth month, changed Minister of Education to Chancellor, yi Grand Tutor Wang Dao was it.
Sixth month, changed Minister of Education to Chancellor, and took Grand Tutor Wang Dao to fill it.
Wikisource transmits 乙太傅王導爲之; 乙 is the graphic stand-in for 以 “take/use,” so the literal line must read the appointment, not the heavenly-stem yi.
On the gengshen day of the seventh month Wang Dao, duke of Shian—credential-bearing palace attendant, chancellor, and inspector of Yangzhou—died.
On the gengshen day of the seventh month Wang Dao, duke of Shixing—credential-bearing palace attendant, chancellor, and inspector of Yangzhou—died.
始興公 is Duke of Shixing; Shian misreads 興.
Autumn, seventh month, day gengshen, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Chancellor, concurrent Inspector of Yangzhou, Duke of Shian Wang Dao died.
Autumn, seventh month, day gengshen, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Chancellor, concurrent Inspector of Yangzhou, Duke of Shixing Wang Dao died.
The same 始興公 must be Shixing in the literal line as well.
Kui An withdrew but swept through eastern Hanzhong, deporting more than seven thousand households to the You and Ji regions.
Kui An withdrew but swept through the country east of the Han, deporting more than seven thousand households to the You and Ji regions.
漢東 is the country east of the Han, not eastern Hanzhong (漢中).
In the third month Empress Yang the martyr was for the first time given joint offerings in Emperor Wu's temple.
In the third month the Wudao Empress Yang was for the first time given joint offerings in Emperor Wu's temple.
武悼 is the posthumous title Wudao, not “martyr”; the replacement restores that title.

Summer, sixth month, day gengyin, the emperor was unwell; an edict stated, "He, with small years, had inherited the great continuation, been entrusted above kings and dukes, and reigned now eighteen years.

Summer, sixth month, day gengyin, the emperor was unwell; an edict stated, "I, with small years, had inherited the great continuation, been entrusted above kings and dukes, and reigned now eighteen years.
朕 is the emperor’s first-person “I” in the edict; “He” reverses the voice.
Prince Yue of Langye, minister of education, is my mother's brother, mature in kindness, with the bearing of a true ruler, and he commands the confidence of the age.
Prince Yue of Langye, minister of education, is my younger brother by the same mother, mature in kindness, with the bearing of a true ruler, and he commands the confidence of the age.
母弟 is a younger brother by the same mother, not a maternal uncle (舅).
Minister of Education, Prince of Langye Yue, in kinship then mother's younger brother, in substance then benevolent and senior, lord-of-men's air, truly fills the age's hope.
Minister of Education, Prince of Langye Yue, in kinship then younger brother by the same mother, in substance then benevolent and senior, lord-of-men's air, truly fills the age's hope.
The literal “mother's younger brother” is English for 舅; 母弟 is uterine younger brother.
He had known nothing of the execution of Prince Zong of Nandun. After Su Jun fell he asked Yu Liang, "Where is the white-haired lord he used to see at court?"
He had known nothing of the execution of Prince Zong of Nandun. After Su Jun fell he asked Yu Liang, "Where is the white-haired lord who was always spoken of?"
常曰白頭公何在 asks where the white-haired lord who was always spoken of is; it does not say the emperor used to see him at court.
In the fourth month of summer Zhou Fu, inspector of Yizhou, and Cao Ju, prefect of Xiyang, attacked Li Shou and routed one of his generals at Jiangyang; the name in the text may stand for Huan.
In the fourth month of summer Zhou Fu, inspector of Yizhou, and Cao Ju, prefect of Xiyang, attacked Li Shou and routed his general Heng at Jiangyang.
敗其將恆于江陽 names the general 恆; dropping the name and guessing 桓 in the idiomatic English is not a translation of this sentence.
The edict closed. Shi Hu then marched against Murong Huang and was crushingly defeated.
Shi Hu marched against Murong Huang and was crushingly defeated.
The unit is only 石季龍帥衆伐慕容皝，皝大敗之; “The edict closed” and “then” are translator glue.

Huan Wen, general who supports the state and interior secretary of Langye, was named junior van commander of the van, given the credential staff, and ordered into Linhuai with his troops. Yu Yi, general who pacifies the west, became grand campaign commander-in-chief and shifted his headquarters to Xiangyang.

Huan Wen, general who supports the state and interior secretary of Langye, was named junior van commander, given the credential staff, and ordered into Linhuai with his troops. Yu Yi, general who pacifies the west, became grand campaign commander-in-chief and shifted his headquarters to Xiangyang.
前鋒小督 is one office, junior van commander; repeating “of the van” restates 前鋒 and muddies the title.
In the first month of spring in the second year of Jianyuan, Zhang Jun dispatched He Lin and Xie Ai against the Southern Qiang in the Khotan region and shattered them.
In the first month of spring in the second year of Jianyuan, Zhang Jun dispatched He Lin and Xie Ai against the Southern Qiang at Tianhe and shattered them.
討南羌于闐和 is locative 于 plus the place 闐和, not the toponym 于闐 (Khotan).
In the fourth month Zhang Guan, serving Zhang Jun, defeated Wang Zhuo of Zhao at Sanjiao city.
In the fourth month Zhang Guan, serving Zhang Jun, defeated Shi Hu's general Wang Zhuo at Sanjiao city.
王擢 is 石季龍將, Shi Hu’s general; “of Zhao” is not in the Chinese.

Initially, when Emperor Cheng was ill, Palace Secretariat Director Yu Bing, considering himself maternal uncle clan holding court, power equal to the lord of men, feared after a different generation, affinal kin would become distant, then said the state had strong enemies, ought to establish a senior lord, thereupon took the emperor as heir.

Initially, when Emperor Cheng was ill, Palace Secretariat Director Yu Bing, considering that as the maternal-uncle house he held the court and that his power equaled the sovereign's, feared that after a change of generations the affinal kin would be distanced; he then said the state had strong enemies and that a mature ruler ought to be established, and thereupon took the emperor as heir.
舅氏當朝，權侔人主 is Yu Bing’s maternal-uncle house dominating court with power rivaling the sovereign; the original literal is ungrammatical and fuses that clause.
Had not armies worthy of Duke Wen of Jin rallied the imperial carriage, and had the dynasty not been tethered like the mulberry at its roots, it would have owed everything to Lord Tao Kan's might.
The imperial carriage was turned back; without hosts like those of Duke Wen of Jin, the dynasty, tethered to the mulberry roots, moreover relied on Lord Tao Kan's strength.
反我皇駕 is a restoration that happened, and 且賴陶公之力 is additional actual reliance on Tao Kan; the original contrary-to-fact turns both into a hypothesis and inverts 且賴.
